title: Inuyashiki
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ichiro Inuyashiki, a 58-year-old man ignored by his family and newly diagnosed with terminal cancer, and teenager Hiro Shishigami are killed and rebuilt as cyborgs by an alien accident. Ichiro uses his powers to heal the sick and stop crime, while Hiro murders strangers, families and police for the thrill of it, and the two finally clash. Kodansha USA published ten volumes; it is a seinen title (rating to verify).
life_message: It holds up compassion and saving others as what makes a person human, whatever body they have.

delivery.evidence: Jason Thompson (ANN) says it plays heroism straight-faced and keeps introducing innocents to be abused; young people drawn as clichéd thugs.
delivery.note: The two cyborgs openly embody opposite views of other people, though Hiro keeps some loyalty to family and friends.

winners_losers: Ichiro wins back his family's respect and saves many, while Hiro and his victims lose, and the online abusers are shown as culpable. Sympathy goes to compassion over power used for thrill.
